prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Labour Party Manifesto 2017 – Summary (≤500 words)

Vision: Build a fairer Britain that works “for the many, not the few,” tackling stagnant wages, insecure work, squeezed public services and regional inequality.

Economy and tax
- National Transformation Fund: £250bn over 10 years for transport, energy, digital and science.
- Fiscal Credibility Rule: eliminate day-to-day deficit within five years; borrow to invest; debt lower by Parliament’s end.
- Fair taxation: no rises in income tax for 95% (under £80k), no NI or VAT hikes; higher taxes for top 5% and large corporations; clamp down on avoidance; protect small firms (lower small profits rate, business rates reform, scrap quarterly reporting for smallest firms).

Industry, finance and ownership
- Industrial strategy with missions: 60% zero/renewable energy and 3% of GDP on R&D by 2030; skills, supply chains, procurement standards; Digital Ambassador.
- National Investment Bank and regional banks to lend £250bn, focus on SMEs and innovation.
- Reform company law (stakeholder duties), takeover protections, curb excessive pay.
- Double co-operative sector; employee “right to own.” Bring rail, energy networks, water and Royal Mail into public ownership over time.

Energy and climate
- Ban fracking; emergency cap to keep average dual-fuel bill under £1,000 while reforming market.
- Public, decentralised energy; insulate 4m homes; support renewables, CCS, tidal; maintain nuclear; protect North Sea jobs.
- Prioritise EU energy market access and Euratom.

Brexit, immigration, trade
- Jobs-first Brexit: close EU relationship, retain benefits of Single Market/Customs Union, reject “no deal,” guarantee EU nationals’ rights.
- Fair, needs-based immigration system; end indefinite detention; crack down on exploitation; restore Migrant Impact Fund.
- Pro-trade: transparency, protect public services and standards, defend steel with trade remedies, boost SME exports.

Education
- National Education Service: cradle-to-grave, free at point of use.
- Early years: expand free hours (incl. 2-year-olds), invest in Sure Start, raise workforce pay/skills.
- Schools: reverse cuts; fair funding; smaller classes for infants; free primary meals funded by VAT on private school fees; reduce high-stakes testing; tackle teacher pay/workload.
- FE/adult: free lifelong learning in colleges; restore EMA; scrap loans/fees for FE; invest in T-levels and pre-apprenticeships.
- Apprenticeships: maintain levy, raise quality and access.
- HE: abolish tuition fees; restore maintenance grants.

Work, welfare and pensions
- 20‑point plan: £10 Living Wage by 2020; ban zero-hours; equal rights from day one; end public sector pay cap; repeal Trade Union Act; tribunal fees abolished; stronger parental and equality rights.
- Social security: scrap sanctions, Bedroom Tax; reform Universal Credit; boost disability support and overhaul assessments.
- Pensions: keep triple lock, bus passes and Winter Fuel Allowance; review state pension age; fair pension charges.

Housing
- Over 1m new homes; at least 100k social homes a year by end of Parliament.
- New Department for Housing; empower councils; new towns; higher standards; protect green belt.
- Private renters: three‑year tenancies, cap rent rises, ban letting fees, tougher standards.
- Suspend Right to Buy where not replaced; end Bedroom Tax; plan to end rough sleeping.

Health and care
- NHS: >£30bn extra over Parliament; scrap pay cap; restore bursaries; end privatisation; meet 18‑week and 4‑hour targets; free hospital parking; improve primary, mental and public health.
- Social care: foundation for a National Care Service; £8bn over Parliament plus long‑term funding plan; Ethical Care Charter; cap lifetime costs and raise asset thresholds.

Safety, justice and communities
- 10,000 more police; tackle VAWG with commissioner, refuge fund; review Prevent.
- 500 more border guards; 3,000 firefighters; statutory flood duty.
- Restore legal aid access; inquiries into historic injustices.
- Prisons/probation: 3,000 more prison officers; end probation privatisation; focus on rehabilitation.
- Support councils, libraries, youth services; Post Bank; protect pubs and limit FOBT stakes to £2.

Transport
- Rail back to public ownership; cap fares; safe staffing; expand electrification/HS2/Crossrail 2; re‑regulate buses; invest in cycling, clean air, ULEVs; fair taxi rules; road safety targets.

Environment and animals
- New Clean Air Act; protect habitats; deposit-return schemes; plant 1m trees.
- End badger cull; tougher cruelty sentences; ban ivory trade; maintain hunting bans.

Culture, media, sport
- £1bn Cultural Capital Fund; free museums; arts pupil premium; fair pay/diversity in creative sectors; protect BBC and Channel 4; implement Leveson.
- Fans’ say in football governance; enforce anti‑touting.

Democracy and equality
- Constitutional Convention; elected second chamber (interim reforms); FOI extension; votes at 16; tougher lobby rules.
- Strong commitments to women’s, LGBT, BAME and disability rights (UNCRPD into law, BSL recognition).

Global Britain
- Diplomacy centred on human rights; recognise Palestine; suspend arms sales for Yemen pending UN probe.
- Defence: spend ≥2% of GDP; renew Trident; modernise capabilities and cyber; support veterans.
- Development: keep 0.7% aid; tackle tax havens; ethical supply chains; global health initiative.
